transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: Tue Feb 2 2027
Start: 10:00 AM PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Rafael, Lena, Connor, Priya, Tomás, Sasha + exec group

Summary:
- Quick state of business: ARR growth holding, some margin pressure, must prioritize reliability investments and targeted hiring.
- Engineering to propose SLO adjustments and resilience runbook updates.
- Product to trim roadmap to focus on conversions and enterprise readiness.
- People Ops to align hiring cadence with budget constraints.

Topics:
1) Reliability & SLOs (incidents, thresholds)
2) Roadmap prioritization and hiring tradeoffs
3) Cost vs latency decisions for hosted vs dedicated customers
4) Compliance & enterprise readiness (audit logs, SOC2 scope)
5) Near-term operational drills and fallout planning

-- Transcript body (timestamps approximate, auto-transcribed, some errors):
[00:00] Maya: Okay, thanks everybody for being here. I'll keep it tight — only an hour but, uh, important items. First, topline from finance, Tomás?
[00:12] Tomás: Yeah, quick update. ARR is up 18% year over year, but gross margin is down about 2 points. Cost of serving is the main driver — GPU spot volatility plus some overprovisioning in Dedicated pools. Finance is asking for a plan to recover 3 points over the next two quarters.
[00:35] Maya: Right, so the ask is, balance short-term margin improvements with no regressions to SLAs. Rafael, thoughts?
[00:42] Rafael: We're seeing a mix. Some customer lanes are very latency-sensitive, they can't be batched aggressively. But for other workloads we can push smarter prefix-caching and tighter batching to trim cost. There's also wins from quantization profiles, but that requires validation on outputs. We can produce an ops plan with conservative rollback windows.
[01:06] Lena: Just to add, product needs to be explicit which features are conversion-pull versus nice-to-have. We should gate brand-new infra changes behind the top three growth bets.
[01:20] Connor: On the reliability front, we hit two P2 incidents in the last 45 days; both were related to autoscaling edge-cases in Dedicated pools during region failover. We need clearer runbooks and a simulated blackout. The SLO windows we use for customer-facing metrics might be too tight for bursty traffic.
[01:41] Maya: Can you propose adjusted SLOs that preserve enterprise SLAs but give us breathing room operationally?
[01:47] Connor: Yes. I'm thinking retain the 99.9% for critical customers but make the internal operational SLOs 99.7% for some lanes to allow for batching/cost tradeoffs. We'll attach clear rollback criteria.
[02:03] Rafael: One caveat — customers often ask for VPC/private deployments, which increases our overhead. Private deployments are a small fraction but they consume capacity and raise support load. Need to price them accordingly.
[02:20] Sasha: From Legal, whatever changes you propose for SLOs, please ensure contract language and SLAs are aligned. And any new telemetry or audits needed for compliance (SOC2/ISO) have to be scoped.
[02:34] Maya: Good point. Tomás, finance: any guardrails on pricing for private?
[02:39] Tomás: We need to maintain a margin floor. If private deployments erode it below threshold, we need to either increase price or reduce included capacity. We can draft tiered pricing for private and dedicated with a clear uplift.
[02:55] -- [02:55] (crosstalk, laughter)
[03:00] Lena: On roadmap, the product org proposes a trimmed list: convert-funnel improvements, evaluation tooling for enterprise signals, and quality monitoring tied to prompt sets. Everything else moves to backlog unless it directly affects conversion or infra stability.
[03:21] Rafael: For the evaluation tooling, we need integration with the Optimize pipeline — if we can surface model/quantization recommendations per-route, that helps customers and reduces cost. But that requires engineering ownership and some compute to run offline evals.
[03:40] Maya: How long to stand up a minimal pipeline?
[03:43] Rafael: We can get an MVP in 6 weeks with two engineers from infra and one from Applied ML, assuming we reassign some capacity.
[03:52] Priya: On hiring, People Ops has a pause on non-essential IC hires until we show the margin improvements. Critical hires — infra SRE and platform security — are still green. We need to prioritize headcount requests.
[04:06] Maya: Okay, so we keep the critical ones. Priya, can you reconcile the hiring request with Finance and present a prioritized list?
[04:12] Priya: Yes, I'll do that and get EM inputs.
[04:17] -- [04:17] (pause)
[04:20] Connor: There's also the ops drill. My ask is 60 minutes of focused chaos testing where we simulate a region outage and test fallback to alternate model variants. We will measure median tail latency, routing correctness, and KV cache warm-up behavior.
[04:38] Lena: I'd like to be in that drill; product will provide the top-5 customer flows to test.
[04:43] Rafael: We'll need a brief pre-run checklist: load profiles, model variants pinned, traffic shaping to avoid collateral customer impact. Also note real customers in Dedicated pools must be notified.
[04:57] Maya: Yes, communications will be required. Sasha, will Legal need specific language to notify customers?
[05:02] Sasha: If it's just a scheduled drill, a courtesy notice is fine. If the drill might impact SLAs, we need clear terms in the contract amendments.
[05:13] -- [05:13] (brief audio glitch)
[05:18] Maya: Okay switching topics, compliance. We have the SOC2 re-audit coming up in Q3. What's the biggest gap?
[05:25] Connor: The audit flagged inconsistent retention policies in a few logging systems and missing proof-of-encryption controls for certain host-based backups. We need to centralize audit logs and show KMS usage across Private deploys.
[05:38] Rafael: For Private deployments, we need a standard KMS integration pattern and documented attestation. That will reduce friction in enterprise sales.
[05:47] Sasha: We'll prepare the SOC2 scoping doc. Need an inventory from infra by next week.
[05:52] Maya: Good. Any risks from competitors we should flag?
[05:55] Lena: Anthropic's enterprise push is shaping conversations and OpenAI keeps moving upmarket with function calling features; we must emphasize reliability and predictable economics.
[06:08] Maya: All right — final section: risk thresholds and escalation. We talked about adjusting SLOs, running the blackout drill, and trimming the roadmap. Let's recap owners.
[06:19] Rafael: I'll take the resilience runbook and SLO proposals.
[06:22] Lena: I'll finalize the trimmed roadmap and the hiring ask deck.
[06:25] Connor: I'll own the blackout drill and the central logging work for SOC2.
[06:28] Priya: I'll align headcount with Finance and circulate the hiring worksheet.
[06:31] Maya: I'll collate and send the Q1 plan by Feb 14.
[06:34] Tomás: Finance will provide the margin guardrails and draft tiered pricing for private by Feb 10.
[06:39] Sasha: Legal will prepare draft contract language for any SLA changes and the customer drill notice template.
[06:44] -- Post-meeting quick Q&A and clarifications:
[06:44] Tomás: On pricing for dedicated, is there appetite to push more to committed reserved capacity?
[06:49] Maya: Yes, push the narrative of committed vs burstable — discounts for reserve. We need to keep a channel for PLG self-serve but make reserved capacity attractive.
[07:00] Lena: For the evaluation tooling, can we include a sample report template that Sales can share to prove cost savings?
[07:06] Rafael: Yes, will include a simple ROI template.
[07:11] -- Closing notes (last 30 seconds):
[07:12] Maya: Thank you all. We will run the drill the week of Feb 15, Rafael and Connor coordinate. Expect the Q1 plan in two weeks. If you're an owner on action items, keep it tight.
[07:27] (meeting end)

Notes about transcription errors: words like "KV cache" sometimes came through as "K-V cash", "Dedicated" became "Dedicat" in a couple spots, and some proper nouns were garbled. Use this transcript as a working artifact and refer to owners for clarifications.
